text:
To bathe one's mane with flour,

to go showing everyone one's shirt,

a sword that does not frighten but provokes laughter,

one's ring, one's watch, and one's chain;


to speak to everyone with a serene face,

to kiss Doña Luisa's feet at mass,

and to attend, as a very necessary matter,

condolence, pleasure, and congratulations;


to be in love with oneself,

to mumble an aria in Italian,

and to dance in French, crooked or straight;


with this, and forgetting the catechism,

behold yourself made a proper courtier,

but the devil will carry you off, said and done.

translation.title: Science of the Courtiers of This Century
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's recipe-like mockery of fashionable courtly behavior.
